question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states that the Parliament consists of the President of India and the two Houses of Parliament known as Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and House of the People (Lok Sabha)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 79**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 79** of the Constitution of India states that the Parliament consists of the President of India and the two Houses of Parliament, namely the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• The President of India is an integral part of the Parliament, although not a member of either House.
 
• The Parliament operates as a bicameral legislature with **Rajya Sabha representing the states and union territories** and **Lok Sabha representing the citizens** through direct elections.
 
• This article is a fundamental provision under **Part V (The Union) and Chapter II (Parliament)** of the Constitution of India.
 
• Article 79 establishes the structure and functioning of the Parliament, ensuring a collaborative legislative process between the President and the two Houses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha (Council of States)**

 
 
• Rajya Sabha is the upper house of Parliament, representing the states and union territories of India.
 
• It is a **permanent body** that is not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every two years.
 
• The **maximum strength** of Rajya Sabha is capped at 250 members as per Article 80 of the Constitution.
 
• The Vice President of India acts as the **ex-officio Chairman** of Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha (House of the People)**
 
 
• Lok Sabha is the lower house of Parliament, with members directly elected by the citizens of India.
 
• The maximum strength of Lok Sabha is **552 members**, including up to 20 members representing Union Territories.
 
• The Speaker of Lok Sabha presides over its sessions and ensures the orderly conduct of business.
 
• It serves as the principal legislative body for **enacting laws** and addressing the needs of the electorate.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President in Parliament**
 
 
• The President summons and prorogues sessions of Parliament and grants assent to bills to convert them into laws.
 
• The President can **dissolve Lok Sabha** and call for fresh elections when necessary.
 
• Under Article 123, the President can issue ordinances when Parliament is not in session.
 
• The President is a crucial part of the legislative process but does not vote or participate in debates.
 
 
 
• **Bicameral Legislature System**
 
 
• India follows a bicameral legislature, consisting of two houses: Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha.
 
• The system ensures **checks and balances** in the legislative process, preventing hasty decisions.
 
• Rajya Sabha focuses on states and union territories, while Lok Sabha represents citizens directly.
 
• Countries like the USA, UK, and Canada also follow bicameral legislature systems.
